stories.title: Mew2King says he will step away after being barred from a Smash event
paragraphs: Super Smash Bros. veteran Jason “Mew2King” Zimmerman was barred from the October 16–17 Xtreme Fighters Showdown in Austin after posts about swollen hands and possible insect bites prompted attendee concerns.

Zimmerman said people had inspected his belongings and found no insects, and he regretted causing alarm. He also said he would stay away from in-person events and streaming for an uncertain period after receiving hostile messages.
The episode became a public safety and personal privacy dispute around a major tournament. The posts did not establish that he had bed bugs or identify what caused the swelling.

scoreNotes.general: A prominent fighting-game figure’s event exclusion escalated into a public dispute and a temporary withdrawal from competition and streaming.
scoreNotes.heat: The XFS decision and Mew2King’s response drew broad fighting-game discussion. The dispute affects an offline tournament and raises questions about how organizers handle possible health risks.
scoreNotes.time: The event ran October 16–17; his response on October 17 added that he would avoid in-person events and streaming for a while.
scoreNotes.ethos: Dexerto reports his statements and the event outcome. The suspected pest and cause of his skin symptoms were not confirmed, so the story does not treat them as fact.

citations.title: Mew2King responds after Smash Bros. Melee event ban over bed bug concerns

stories.title: Jynxzi’s creator-run League tournament peaked at 414,000 viewers
paragraphs: Streamer Nicholas “Jynxzi” Stewart’s second League of Legends creator tournament peaked at 414,000 concurrent viewers across its broadcasts on October 14, according to Streams Charts.

The event recorded 1.9 million hours watched over a little more than six hours and brought together 40 streamers. Riot Games backed the tournament again, with Twitch Drops including an Arcane Warwick skin.
The peak was below the first edition’s 920,800, but Streams Charts says the October event still matched or exceeded recent audiences for major regional leagues. Its figures remain preliminary.

scoreNotes.general: A large streamer-led competition again drew an audience comparable to established regional esports leagues.
scoreNotes.heat: The October 14 event peaked at 414,000 concurrent viewers, generated 1.9 million hours watched, and included 40 creators. These are substantial measured signals, even though the first edition was larger.
scoreNotes.time: The tournament took place October 14 and was reported October 15, so it qualifies as a new-to-Owl seven-day story rather than a development in the last 24 hours.
scoreNotes.ethos: Streams Charts reports preliminary cross-broadcast audience figures and identifies Riot Games’ support and Twitch Drops. The report notes that final figures may change.

stories.title: PaymoneyWubby reignites debate over Twitch’s subscription split
paragraphs: Streamer PaymoneyWubby called Twitch’s usual 50/50 subscription split “highway robbery” and argued creators have better revenue terms on rival Kick, where he says the split is 95/5.

The remarks revived discussion over how creators balance per-subscriber income with platform reach and business models. In the sampled Reddit threads, some viewers favored creators receiving more of each subscription, while others questioned whether a higher share compensates for a smaller audience or Kick’s reliance on gambling advertising.
This is a creator’s argument about platform economics, not evidence that Twitch is changing its payout policy.

scoreNotes.general: A large streamer’s criticism renewed a persistent creator-business debate, with viewers weighing payout against audience reach and platform trade-offs.
scoreNotes.heat: The report drew active discussion across Twitch-focused communities. The sampled Reddit threads showed disagreement over whether a larger share on Kick outweighs differences in audience size, platform economics, and its gambling advertising.
scoreNotes.time: Wubby’s comments and the sampled discussion date to October 14, inside the seven-day fallback window but not the preceding 24 hours.
scoreNotes.ethos: Dexerto attributes the comments to Wubby and describes the standard Twitch split as 50/50, with some contract exceptions. Reddit comments are a limited sample, not a measure of all creators or viewers.

stories.title: Livestream viewing hit a quarterly record as TikTok LIVE and Kick grew
paragraphs: Streams Charts says services in its tracking set generated a record 31.7 billion livestream hours in Q3 2026, up 0.8% from the prior quarter.

TikTok LIVE grew 19% to 10.6 billion hours and a 33.5% share of the tracked market. Kick grew 30.7% to 2.04 billion hours, while Twitch rose 4% to 4.51 billion; YouTube remained largest but its share fell from 49.5% to 43%.

The comparison points to rising competition for creator audiences, especially as Kick closes some of the viewing gap with Twitch. Viewing hours do not show how much creators earned or how audiences feel about each platform.

scoreNotes.general: The quarter’s viewing totals show a shifting competitive landscape for creator distribution, with strong movement among the largest live platforms.
scoreNotes.heat: Streams Charts measured a record 31.7 billion hours watched across its tracked services; TikTok LIVE reached 33.5% share and Kick grew 30.7% quarter over quarter. The data indicates attention, not revenue or creator earnings.
scoreNotes.time: This seven-day report covers Q3, which ended before the current 24-hour window; the release is new to Owl but the underlying quarter is not.
scoreNotes.ethos: The figures are from Streams Charts’ cross-platform measurement and are limited to services it tracks. They do not establish total global viewing or financial performance.

stories.title: Liquid Swords enters bankruptcy as its game and assets go up for sale
paragraphs: Swedish studio Liquid Swords, founded by former Avalanche co-founder Christofer Sundberg and developer-publisher of Samson, was placed into bankruptcy by a Stockholm court on October 12, according to reports published this week.

Kotaku, citing Swedish business outlet Breakit via Gametalk, reports that the studio employed close to 30 people and that staff had not been paid since August. The bankruptcy administrator has put the studio and its assets, including Samson, up for sale, with bidding scheduled to close October 21.

Samson launched to poor reviews and reported bugs, but the studio had continued issuing updates. The sale will determine whether the game receives further support; no buyer or outcome was confirmed in the checked reporting.

scoreNotes.general: The bankruptcy puts a roughly 30-person studio and the future of its only released game in question, illustrating the commercial risks around a troubled launch.
scoreNotes.heat: Liquid Swords’ closure is consequential for its staff and for Samson’s support. The developer’s assets, including the game, are reportedly being offered for sale, with a bid deadline approaching.
scoreNotes.time: The court order was issued October 12 and the story was reported October 15–17. This is a new-to-Owl seven-day development, not a last-24-hour event.
scoreNotes.ethos: Kotaku cites Swedish outlet Breakit and Gametalk for the court order, staffing and unpaid wages. Breakit’s page exposed only its paywalled title and date here; details are attributed to the reporting chain, not independently confirmed.

stories.title: An indie studio canceled a public demo over fears of fast AI copycats
paragraphs: Alliance Arts and WHO YOU canceled the planned October 19 public demo for Drunken Goddess Reflux, replacing it with a limited online playtest whose participants must agree to rules on posting and streaming footage.

The developers said they could not reliably manage the planned restrictions on public gameplay footage and feared that a visible demo could help others use AI or other tools to reproduce its presentation and mechanics before the original game launches.
GamesRadar placed the game at No. 65 on Steam’s wishlists. The decision comes amid other reported pre-release lookalikes, but the developers did not say that this title had already been copied.

scoreNotes.general: A highly wishlisted indie game changed its launch promotion in response to fears that a public demo could enable fast-follow copies, raising a concrete distribution issue for small studios.
scoreNotes.heat: The game was reported among Steam’s top 65 wishlisted titles and its decision drew substantial public discussion. The wider significance is a developer changing public access to reduce copying risk.
scoreNotes.time: The change was announced October 16 and reported October 16–17, within the collection’s 24-hour window based on the dated reports.
scoreNotes.ethos: The studio’s Steam statement is quoted by GamesRadar and Inven Global. The developers cited both difficulty enforcing video restrictions and concern about AI-assisted imitation; no copy of this specific game was reported.

stories.title: Steam Next Fest begins October 19 with demos and developer streams
paragraphs: Steam Next Fest’s October edition runs October 19–26, giving players access to demos of upcoming PC games and opportunities to watch developer streams and offer feedback.
Valve says participating games must have a public store page and playable demo, and must be scheduled to release after the festival ends. A game can take part in only one Next Fest.

The event is a concentrated discovery window for unreleased titles and a chance for smaller teams to gather early player feedback. Valve’s event page does not provide a total for participating games or expected viewers.

scoreNotes.general: Steam’s upcoming festival is a major discovery and feedback window for unreleased games, particularly relevant to developers seeking visibility ahead of launch.
scoreNotes.heat: The official event covers demos, developer streams and player feedback across participating upcoming games. The checked sources establish the event’s scope but no participant or audience total.
scoreNotes.time: Valve schedules the week-long event for October 19–26, immediately after this edition’s window. The event date is upcoming, not a new announcement in the last 24 hours.
scoreNotes.ethos: Valve’s Steamworks documentation confirms the dates, format and eligibility rules. No participation total or audience forecast was provided.

research.note: All 13 planned discovery searches and five topic fallbacks were completed. Creator searches began with mostly stale or generic results; flexible recovery and follow-up queries surfaced supported leads. Viewership totals are third-party measures, and some reports are several days old.
